brief: A tool caddy with a carry handle and divided bins for screws and bits.

requirements.evidence: Three full bases in a row: piece:-1,0,0, piece:0,0,0 and piece:1,0,0. Open faces are capped and the joints between cells are bolted (jointBolt x2).

handle:0,0,0;top sits on cover:0,0,0;full;top over the middle cell, so the caddy's weight is balanced either side of the handle. The configurator checks fit only. It can't tell how much weight the handle will hold, which depends on the material you print in.
bin:-1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 has 3 compartments, staged with M3 screws, nuts and standoffs.
bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div2 has 2 compartments for bits. The catalogue has no bit prop, so I staged it with a heap of screws and a heap of nuts as a stand-in.

finish.summary: I built a three-cell tool caddy in a straight row. The middle cell has a top cover with a carry handle on it. The two end cells hold divided bins: a full-depth 3-compartment bin on the west end and a full-depth 2-compartment bin on the east end. I capped every open face with solid end caps and bolted the joints between the cells. That makes 30 parts and an estimated 1628 g of filament. check_build passes with no rule issues, and the mesh-collision check reads clear. To show what it's for, I put small heaps of M3 screws, nuts and standoffs in the compartments. They sit below the bin rims, so you can see them from above but not from the side. The prop catalogue has no screwdriver bits, so I used a heap of nuts as a stand-in for bits in the 2-compartment bin. I tried standing a hex driver and a screwdriver up in that bin, but the configurator wouldn't place them.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
